tex_content.html:
\begin{example} \end{example}[Fundamental solution of Schrödinger's equation] ↗ thm:plancherel-theorem ↗ ex:fourier-transform-heat-fundamental-solution 1. ch4:4.3.1-ex-3\group Fourier Transform

For $iu_t+\Delta u=0$, formally continue the heat kernel to $it$: \[ u(x,t)=\frac1{(4\pi it)^{n/2}}\int _{\R ^n}e^{i|x-y|^2/(4t)}g(y)\, dy. \] This solves the equation for suitable $g$, and Plancherel gives $\| u(\cdot ,t)\| _2=\| g\| _2$, extending the formula from $L^1\cap L^2$ to $L^2$. \end{example}
